newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sandvik says to redeem shares worth 4.0 bln Skr. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sandvik says to redeem shares worth 4.0 bln Skr. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Swedish tool and engineering group Sandvik said on Monday it would redeem shares worth 4.0 billion crowns at three percent under market price.

Sandvik's largest shareholder, construction company Skanska, has undertaken to place as many shares at Sandvik's disposal as is necessary to enable the proposed redemption to be carried out in full, the company said in a statement.
If the share price falls below 170 crowns a shares, Sandvik and Skanska have the right to withdraw the redemption proposal, the company said.
Investment company Industrivarden will vote in favour of the redemption, Sandvik said.
Industrivarden is buying 22 million Sandvik A series shares at a price of 185 crowns each, excluding the proposed 1996 dividend, for a total of 4.1 billion crowns.
Sandvik A shares fell eight crowns to 185 crowns at the open on Monday. Its B shares plunged 25.5 crowns at the open but quickly recovered to be 6.5 crowns lower at 187 crowns at 0830 GMT.
As the redemption price per share will be lower than the market price, Sandvik cautioned that other shareholders should carefully consider if they want to participate.
The decision to reduce the share capital will be taken by an extraordinary general meeting, which is planned to be held on June 9, the company said in a statement.
"Following Sandvik's favourable profitability and cash flow in recent years, some overcapitalisation has been created," Sandvik said.
"In view of this a decision has previously been taken on a revised dividend policy implying a significant increase in dividends."
The company said it had also awaited legislation allowing share buy backs, but as such legislation remained uncertain it had decided to investigate alternative measures.
"The proposed terms of the redemption are designed to create an improved capital structure and thereby create possibilities for an increased shareholder value," Sandvik said.

"Sandvik's future cash flow, together with the new capital base is considered to be sufficient to run and expand the operations in accordance with Sandvik's strategy as well as maintaining the new dividend policy."
The share redemption will decrease liquid assets by two billion crowns and increase interest-bearing debts by the remaining amount, the company said.
The application period will run from May 7 to May 22.
